speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, at what age did you first notice the stridor and wheezing in your infant, and have these episodes been triggered specifically by crying, feeding, or cold air?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia.

Based on the clinical history of an infant with stridor and wheezing exacerbated by crying, feeding, and neck flexion, along with post-prandial vomiting, the findings are highly characteristic of laryngomalacia. This is the most common cause of congenital stridor in infants.
